en: If the punishment has no verifiable reason or reasonable path of challenge, its review or reversal may be due. The request may also include that the network create or improve a real path for you to defend yourself.

When the same punishment policy hits many accounts without explanation, the response can be collective and reach the whole punishment system. Procon, Consumidor.gov.br, the Public Prosecutor's Office and the Public Defender's Office can act in these cases.

The network has the power to punish and to organise what appears, but that power alone is not enough. It needs a verifiable reason, consistency from one decision to the next and an understandable path of challenge.
<1>What to ask the network for after the punishment or the drop?</1>
1. On a social network, what you see and how many people see what you post, the so-called reach, depend on the platform's own rules.
2. There may be a problem when the change alters the logic of visibility, the reputation criteria or the rules of circulation.
3. Your access, your permanence, your visibility and your chance to complain may depend on punishments nobody explains.
What can you ask for when the rule was not properly disclosed?

Outside the company, the next step is Procon, Consumidor.gov.br or the Small Claims Court. When the same rule affects all customers, the correction can come for everyone, through the action of public consumer protection bodies.
<1>What can you ask for when the rule was not properly disclosed?</1>
1. There may be too much text, so that the essential gets lost among the rest, or the rule may be spread across documents, screens and menus that do not connect.
2. Being written somewhere is not enough, because what counts is whether, at the moment of deciding, you could understand what that rule meant.
3. The question, then, is whether the rule appeared clearly and at the moment it could change your decision to buy, to continue or to react.
What to ask for when staying and leaving are both costly?

If it does not answer, the complaint can go to Procon, Consumidor.gov.br or the Small Claims Court. The cost of leaving is usually the same for all users. So the response can apply to everyone, through a collective action or through the public consumer protection bodies.
Not every intense relationship with a game is a problem, and keeping customers with challenges and rewards is not unlawful in itself. What counts is when this demonstrably raises the cost of leaving.
<1>What to ask for when staying and leaving are both costly?</1>
1. You think about quitting the game, the network or the service, but leaving means losing the rank, the reputation, the history and the ties that only exist inside.
2. Here it is different, because the history, the rank, the signs of prestige and the bonds you made stay with the company and are only worth something inside.
3. The clearest sign appears when the company changes the rules and you accept only because leaving would cost more.

The basis of proof is the description of the plan or offer on the day you signed up, with what was included. Dated screenshots showing the before and after also help. The change notices the company sent count too, because it should have told you the essentials in time for you to understand and react.

The complaint starts with the company itself, and continuing to pay does not mean you accepted the deterioration. When the change is relevant, it should have been communicated understandably, and your silence does not count as agreement.

When the deterioration hits all customers at the same time, it is the kind of problem that can go to Procon, the Public Defender's Office or the Public Prosecutor's Office. In these cases the response can correct the service for everyone, and not just repair your case.
1. The name and the price stayed the same, and what shrank was the delivery.
2. The shell of the service can stay intact while the content has been emptied.
3. A one-day fluctuation or a small adjustment is not enough, and not every reduction is unlawful.

It happens when you complain about something that disappeared or got worse and the answer is that you never had anything, because it was all a permission that could disappear. Things without a body are also assets in law, and when there was real payment the word licence is not enough to erase what you received.

First come the payment receipt and the purchase screen with the word the button used. A capture of the inventory or library with what is in your account also helps. This shows that you decided in the language of purchase, even if the contract speaks of a licence.
1. You paid, the button said buy, and the contract calls what you received a licence, a permission of use that can be withdrawn.
2. It is how much what you use depends on an environment the platform maintains, adjusts and can change.
3. The name the contract gives does not on its own decide your protection, because consumer law also treats as a product what has no body.

The main piece is the screen that described the draw, with the odds, the guarantee by number of attempts, the spending cap and the deadline. The official description itself is important evidence, because it shows the path to the item was designed as a series of paid attempts, and not as a direct purchase.
What can you demand from whoever sells the draw?

If it does not resolve things, there remain Procon, Consumidor.gov.br and the Small Claims Court, each with its own pace and cost. Since the draw is the same for everyone, a problem in its design tends to hit many people, and the response can come through a collective action or through public consumer protection bodies.
<1>What can you demand from whoever sells the draw?</1>
1. This is one of the most sensitive points of consumption in games, because the one who decides the odds, the currency, the rarity and the deadlines is the company itself.
2. The value of what you take home comes to depend on internal rules of distribution, availability and rarity that only the company defines, often together with time windows and signs of scarcity.
3. When direct purchase disappears and the draw becomes mandatory, you stop choosing how to reach the item and start paying to try.
What can you ask for when the app changes the rule?

The request may include that the app keep and show the minimum records, explain the restrictions verifiably and review the criteria used to restrict. It may also include clarity about what defines the distribution of calls and the restoration of what the change made worse.

When the same change hits everyone who works on the app, the response can be collective and ask for minimum criteria of distribution and priority for all. The Public Prosecutor's Office and the Public Defender's Office can act in these cases.
<1>What can you ask for when the app changes the rule?</1>
1. You do deliveries or rides through an app and, after a rule change nobody explained, calls decreased, earnings fell or a restriction arrived.
2. The one who distributes calls, calculates earnings, gives ratings, decides priority and applies restrictions is the app.
3. Even so, they can significantly empty the earnings that justified staying.

When consumer law reaches those who sell, it applies above all to the platform's commercial practices and to the contract clauses. In the face of a punishment, a verifiable reason and a real path of challenge also weigh.
1. Earning an income through the platform does not, in itself, remove this protection.
2. Those who sell depend on the ranking, reputation and prominence the platform controls.
3. What weighs is how much the platform governs your presence on it.
